html:
SMTO-AUT-0008 — This connection doesn't allow the access SMTO needs

GUID: c23358f0-69cd-57d2-83b5-705498b2f34f
Slug: auth-additional-scope-required
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • This action needs access that the saved connection isn't set up to allow, or that wasn't approved when you signed in. SMTO can't add that access on its own, so it stopped before using the connection.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who set up this connection to add the missing permission to the allowed permissions in its app entry in Parameter Store. SMTO can only ask for permissions that the connection's settings allow; a Task can't add more.
  2. When SMTO shows Open authorization page, sign in and approve every permission the service lists, without unticking any. If one is left unapproved, the service grants less access than this action needs and the error comes back.
  3. If the step was making a change, check whether it already happened, then ask SMTO in the conversation to try it again. Checking first avoids making the same change twice once the access is in place.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in finishes and the step continues without asking for more access.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Ask them to add only the permissions this action needs, and never share sign-in codes or passwords.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OAuth broker found that the requested, default or operation-required scopes (or the resource/audience) are outside the client's allowed_scopes, or are not among the connection's granted_scopes.

What this means

  • Requested/default/required scopes exceed the client's allowlist or the connection's recorded granted scopes. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Requested/default/required scopes exceed the client's allowlist or the connection's recorded granted scopes.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare required scopes with both the client allowlist and recorded consent; identify which boundary lacks permission.

How to fix it

  • Compare the operation's required_scopes with the oauth2_client allowed_scopes and default_scopes, and with the oauth2_connection requested_scopes, granted_scopes and resource/audience, in Parameter Store. Add only the scopes this operation needs to allowed_scopes, then re-authorize so the provider grants them; tool arguments cannot expand scopes.
  • Review the client allowlist and connection scopes in Parameter Store, then authorize again. Tool arguments cannot expand scopes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • Only the intended required scopes are allowed by the client and present in the authorized connection.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
